mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep drifting upward from their current depressed levels, commuting-linked spending will expand and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism is a gradual return of weekday travel and lunchtime shopping that directly increases retail visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise week over week for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL use suppresses outside shopping trips as more time is spent at home, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks. The effect is strongest when RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay weak.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 11 points above baseline for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior 4-week mean within 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated and both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES not improving.

mechanism_narrative: An acceleration in GROCERY_PHARM indicates routine essential trips are substituting for discretionary retail visits, so RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks. This is a demand reallocation mechanism rather than a total mobility expansion.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases by at least 1 point week-on-week for two straight weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher than its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising week over week for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed, access to shopping districts stays constrained and retail visits weaken over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if transit usage rebounds enough to restore city-center access.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -18 for the full current week and the next week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the previous 4-week average within 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -18 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS use signals warmer outdoor conditions and more overall footfall, which spills into nearby retail trips and lifts RETAIL_REC within one week. The effect is immediate because the same weather shock raises both outdoor leisure and shopping activity.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the following week after a week-on-week PARKS rise of at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: If RETAIL_REC stops improving while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, households are consolidating trips and avoiding discretionary shopping, so retail mobility will remain below its prior four-week average over the next two weeks. This mechanism is a home-centering response, not a transit response.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains below -12 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 11
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean within 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 11.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT creates more weekday exposure to retail corridors, producing a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next four weeks. The mechanism requires both series to improve together; one without the other is not enough.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -9 while TRANSIT rises above -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT cross the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening conditions, a stable but still negative TRANSIT trend no longer drags retail activity down because people substitute local walking and neighborhood shopping, so RETAIL_REC edges upward over the next four weeks. The signal is conditional on restrictions not tightening again.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls below its last 4-week mean over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains roughly flat and restrictions do not tighten.
